turns.content: Consider SMEFT built from Standard Model fields and higher-dimensional operators in a local, unitary, Lorentz-invariant quantum field theory on Minkowski spacetime, with no explicitly spacetime-dependent Wilson coefficients. Before deciding which symmetries every operator must respect, distinguish symmetries built into this framework from discrete symmetries that may be violated.
Under these assumptions, why must every SMEFT operator respect Lorentz symmetry?
Do the same assumptions also require Poincare invariance? Account for translations as well as Lorentz transformations.
Is CP a mandatory symmetry of every SMEFT operator, or may SMEFT contain CP-violating operators? Explain.
Apply the CPT theorem to this local, unitary, Lorentz-invariant theory. What does it imply for SMEFT operators?
Classify Lorentz, Poincare, CP, and CPT symmetries as mandatory or optional in this framework.
Explain why allowing CP violation is compatible with CPT and does not conflict with Poincare invariance.
State the final set of symmetries that every SMEFT operator must respect under the assumptions above.
